title: Adverbs
subtitle: прилагательные и наречия: форма, смысл, позиция, степени сравнения

ruleBlocks.text: Adjective описывает существительное или состояние после глагола-связки, а adverb описывает действие, другое прилагательное или другое наречие. Самый быстрый вопрос: если это какой? -> adjective, если как? -> adverb.

ruleBlocks.caption: Какой вопрос задаем
rows: The weather is fine. You look great.

ruleBlocks.title: Базовая формула
lines: Чаще всего: adverb = adjective + -ly (complete -> completely, simple -> simply, wonderful -> wonderfully, global -> globally).
Не каждое слово на -ly - наречие: friendly, lovely, lively, silly, cowardly - это прилагательные.
Смысл важнее формы: один и тот же корень может давать разные части речи в зависимости от контекста.

ruleBlocks.text: Adjectives на -ly: обычно без формы adverb

ruleBlocks.caption: Как сказать правильно
rows: in a lovely way / in a lovely manner

ruleBlocks.text: Tricky pairs: без -ly и с -ly дают разный смысл
После глаголов-связок обычно употребляются прилагательные, а не наречия: appear, be, become, feel, get, grow, look, seem, smell, sound, taste, turn.

items.ru: feel как linking verb -> adjective bad.

ruleBlocks.text: Те же глаголы могут быть смысловыми

ruleBlocks.caption: Сравни: linking vs action
rows: The chef tasted the sauce carefully.
He turned quickly at the corner.

ruleBlocks.title: Особый случай: well
lines: to be well / to look well: well = adjective здоровый (I am well. She looks well today.).
You cook well: здесь well = adverb хорошо, описывает действие cook.
feel good чаще про эмоциональное состояние; feel well чаще про физическое самочувствие.

ruleBlocks.caption: Comparative / Superlative
rows: fast -> faster -> fastest; early -> earlier -> earliest
more quickly -> most quickly; more seldom -> most seldom
less often -> least often; less effectively -> least effectively
well -> better -> best; badly -> worse -> worst; much -> more -> most; little -> less -> least

ruleBlocks.text: SO, SUCH, ENOUGH, TOO и позиция ALSO / TOO / AS WELL / EITHER

ruleBlocks.caption: Шаблоны, которые часто путают
rows: This smartphone is so expensive. Why are you walking so slowly?
It was such an amazing experience. She posted such lovely pictures.
There are so many options. You've eaten so little.
I've put on such a lot of weight!
old enough; fast enough; know enough
The coffee is too hot. She made too many mistakes.
I'd like to believe him, too. He knows the truth as well.
I can't swim. I can't dive either.
обычно перед смысловым глаголом; после am/is/are/was/were
She also goes to the gym. Information is also available online.

ruleBlocks.title: Чек-лист перед ответом
lines: Если слово описывает действие (run, speak, explain, work), обычно нужен adverb.
Проверь ловушки: hard/hardly, late/lately, near/nearly, close/closely, high/highly.
Помни позицию enough (после adjective/adverb/verb; перед noun) и too (перед словом, которое усиливает).
also обычно стоит перед смысловым глаголом, а too/as well/either - чаще в конце предложения.

ruleBlocks.title: Связанные темы
ruleBlocks.note: После этого правила полезно закрепить Simple/Continuous и глаголы состояния.

items.prompt: She plays the guitar so good that her videos often go viral online.
accepted: She plays the guitar so well that her videos often go viral online.
She plays guitar so well that her videos often go viral online.
items.explain: good -> well, потому что описываем play.

items.prompt: The cheetah runs incredibly fastly, making it the perfect hunter in the wild.
accepted: The cheetah runs incredibly fast, making it the perfect hunter in the wild.
The cheetah runs incredibly fast and is the perfect hunter in the wild.

items.prompt: It was obviously that he didn't study for the test.
accepted: It was obvious that he didn't study for the test.

items.prompt: The movie was bad written, but the actors gave decent performances.
accepted: The movie was badly written, but the actors gave decent performances.

items.prompt: The traffic was moving so slow that I had enough time to finish a podcast episode.
accepted: The traffic was moving so slowly that I had enough time to finish a podcast episode.

accepted: That documentary was so interesting that I forgot to check my phone.

items.prompt: The customer service representative was incredibly politely and solved my issue quickly.
